documents.title: Rheumatology follow up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just an update since I don't think rheum sends you their notes after the first one. Saw them on the 27th. My wrists are still sore and stiff for a good hour plus every morning, a little better than before but not much. New thing is my thumb, pointer and middle fingers go numb and tingly, mostly at night - it woke me up a couple times. When the doctor bent my wrists down and held them for a minute it brought the tingling right on. They did x-rays of both hands and said the bones are a bit thin around the joints and there are some early erosions, which I didn't love hearing. They kept me on the same methotrexate, folic acid and prednisone and want to see me in a few months. Should I be doing anything else?

documents.title: RE: Rheumatology follow up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for filling me in, that's really helpful. The finger tingling can come from swelling at the wrist pressing on the nerve, and it often settles as the arthritis gets controlled. Rheumatology is the right team to steer the RA treatment, so keep that follow-up. If the numbness becomes constant or you notice weakness or dropping things, let me know. I'll see you in March and we'll do your pneumonia vaccine then.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: legs at night.

HPI: Since around November she gets a creeping, unpleasant feeling deep in both lower legs in the evening, mostly once she's in bed, with a strong need to move them. Walking to the kitchen or stretching fixes it for a while, then it comes back. Husband says she kicks. Takes her a long time to fall asleep now. No back pain, no leg weakness, no cramps per se, no calf swelling.

RA: on MTX 15 weekly, folic acid, pred 5 via rheumatology. Mornings somewhat better than in the fall. Finger tingling at night still comes and goes.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Wrists mildly boggy bilaterally, less than September. Legs: no edema, calves soft, pedal pulses 2+. Strength and reflexes normal in the legs, sensation intact to light touch.

A/P
1. Nocturnal leg discomfort with urge to move, relieved by movement - sounds like restless legs. Referring to neurology; they can check iron and confirm.
2. RA on MTX/pred - per rheum.
3. Hypothyroidism - stable.
4. PCV20 today given immunosuppressive therapy. Tolerated.
Physical in September.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every other day with orange juice
medications.reason: Restless legs syndrome with low ferritin

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology outpatient consult, 05/01/2023.

53-year-old woman with RA on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone and treated hypothyroidism, referred for leg symptoms. For roughly six months she has had a deep, crawling discomfort in the legs and an urge to move them, worst in the evening and at night, eased for a time by walking or stretching. She has no back pain, weakness or numbness in the legs.

Neurological examination is normal. Peripheral pulses intact.

Labs: hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, ferritin 15 ng/mL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, TSH 2.5 mIU/L.

Assessment: restless legs syndrome. Ferritin is well below the level we aim for in RLS.

Recommendations: ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day, taken with vitamin C and away from levothyroxine by at least 4 hours. Repeat ferritin in about 3 months. Sleep hygiene discussed. Will see again as needed.

Neurology Clinic

documents.title: Referral question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is a little embarrassing. For about six months I've had really bad itching down below, on the outside, and it's worst at night. I've gone through a few tubes of the drugstore yeast cream and it hasn't touched it. No discharge, no bleeding. I'd rather see a gynecologist for this - can you put in a referral? The insurance needs one from you.

documents.title: RE: Referral question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not embarrassing at all, and it makes sense to have gynecology take a proper look since the yeast creams haven't helped. Referral placed today. If you notice any sores, bleeding or a lump before then, message me and I'll get you in here sooner.

conditions.label: Lichen sclerosus
conditions.note: clinical diagnosis by gynecology 06/22/2023; biopsy planned

documents.title: Saw the gynecologist
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw GYN yesterday. She said the skin on the vulva and around the back is thin and crinkly with white patches, and she thinks it is lichen sclerosus. No swollen glands. She wants to do a small biopsy at my next visit in August to be sure. Until then she said I can use the over the counter hydrocortisone. Just wanted you to have it for my chart.

documents.title: RE: Saw the gynecologist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you, added to your problem list as a working diagnosis. The biopsy is the right next step. Hope the itching eases a bit in the meantime.

reports.text:
Specimen: vulva, punch biopsy, submitted 08/21/2023 by outpatient gynecology. Clinical history: pruritus, white atrophic patches.

Microscopic: the epidermis is thinned with compact hyperkeratosis. The upper dermis shows a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate. No atypia.
reports.conclusion: Hyperkeratosis, atrophic epidermis and band-like dermal lymphocytic infiltrate, consistent with lichen sclerosus. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: Pathology copy received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Copy of vulvar biopsy pathology (collected 8/21) faxed by the gynecology office at pt's request. Scanned, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Pathology reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Biopsy confirms lichen sclerosus, no dysplasia. Gyn managing; she has follow-up with them in October.

medications.reason: patient stopped in August for constipation

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53F, annual.

Since last year: RA dx'd by rheumatology Oct 2022, on MTX 15 mg weekly + folate + pred 5. Hands are better, stiffness down to maybe 30-40 min. Restless legs dx'd by neurology in May with ferritin 15; started iron every other day but stopped in August because she was badly constipated. Legs still bother her a few nights a week. Lichen sclerosus on vulvar biopsy in August, gyn following, still itchy at night on OTC hydrocortisone, sees them again in October.

Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg, prednisone 5 mg.

Exam: well. Thyroid normal. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Hands with mild wrist fullness, no deformity. Skin fine. Legs no edema. GU exam deferred, gyn following.

A/P
1. RLS, low ferritin, off iron for GI side effects. Discussed retrying with a stool softener or a gentler preparation; she'd like a break for now and will bring it up with neurology. Not pushing today.
2. RA - per rheum, labs through their office.
3. Hypothyroidism - TSH.
4. Lichen sclerosus - per gyn.
5. HM: mammogram ordered. Flu/COVID at a nurse visit next month. PHQ-2 1.
CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH today.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs reviewed, nothing actionable. TSH in range. Portal note sent.

medications.sig: Apply a thin layer to the affected vulvar skin nightly for 4 weeks, then twice weekly

documents.title: Fill history update
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External fill history shows clobetasol 0.05% ointment 30 g dispensed 10/23/2023, prescriber outpatient gynecology. Added to med list as an outside prescription.

documents.title: GYN follow up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update for my file. The hydrocortisone never really helped and the itching is still worst at night. GYN said there is some scarring now and the inner lips have changed shape, which was upsetting. No swollen glands. She said the biopsy from August already answers it so no new one. I'm starting a strong steroid ointment every night for a month and then twice a week to keep it quiet. Back to see her in a year or sooner if it flares.

documents.title: RE: GYN follow up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Jennifer. Clobetasol is the standard treatment and most people get real relief from it. I've added it to your list. Use only a thin layer, as she showed you.

documents.body: Flu (L deltoid) and 2023-24 COVID (R deltoid). Took her methotrexate on Saturday as usual. Observed 15 min, fine.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing ok. The clobetasol made a big difference, itching mostly gone, using it twice a week now as directed. Joints: some mornings stiff, manageable, still on the same RA regimen; saw rheum in January and they're content. RLS a few nights a week, she gets up and walks; did not restart iron. Tingling in fingers rare now.

O: vitals ok. Wrists without effusion today. Heart, lungs normal.

A/P
Hypothyroidism: TSH, continue.
RA: per rheum.
Lichen sclerosus: controlled on maintenance clobetasol per gyn.
RLS: ongoing, she declines iron retrial for now.
Physical in September, Pap due then.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 54F. Feels well overall.

Problems:
- Hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 100 mcg.
- Seropositive erosive RA on MTX 15 weekly, folic acid, prednisone 5 (rheum). Joints fairly quiet.
- RLS, no current treatment, symptoms tolerable.
- Vulvar lichen sclerosus on clobetasol twice weekly (gyn), well controlled.

Exam: well. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: external exam per gyn, speculum exam with normal-appearing cervix, Pap/HPV collected. Hands without synovitis today. Skin ok.

A/P
Routine labs, TSH.
Pap/HPV today.
Mammogram ordered.
Colonoscopy due 2026 (10 yr from 2016).
Flu and COVID shots next month.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Annual results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs back, released. Pap negative, HPV negative - next co-test in 5 years. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu L deltoid, 2024-25 COVID R deltoid. No issues. Pt mentioned she had her yearly gyn visit last week - skin controlled on twice-weekly ointment, no changes made. Noted for PCP.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with prior exams back to 2021. Heterogeneously dense parenchyma. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion.
